raw_case_text: A 48-year-old male patient was diagnosed with stage II HIV infection 11 years back after presenting with cutaneous fungal infections. He was treated with topical antifungals, and started on ART (AZT-3TC-EFV) and cotrimoxazole preventive therapy (CPT) with a baseline CD4+ count 175 cells/mm3. The patient achieved an undetected viral load after 6 months of ART initiation. The ART regimen was shifted to TDF-3TC-DTG after 10 years as recommended by the National Comprehensive HIV Care Guideline. His fasting blood sugar (FBS) level was 101 mg/dl at time of the DTG-based ART initiation. He was told to have hypertension on medical follow up and was prescribed amlodipine, 10 mg po daily, and advised on lifestyle modification. He was diagnosed to have diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) with clinical evidence of polyuria, polydipsia and fatigue, severe hyperglycemia (RBS=320-466 mg/dl, HbA1c=9.3%), and ketonuria (3+)), which occurred after 7 months of DTG-based ART regimen (Table 1). No documented preceding infections. No personal or family history of diabetes mellitus or dyslipidemia. Serum C-peptide level, anti-insulin antibody or anti-glutamic acid decarboxylase (GAD) antibody were not determined due to limited clinical setup. He was treated with intravenous fluids, regular insulin and IV KCl, and recovered from DKA after 4 days of admission. NPH insulin 20/10 IU s/c daily was started, which later changed to metformin 850 mg/day. Good glycemic control (FBS=101-130 mg/dl, HbA1c=7.1%) was obtained with metformin, while the DTG-based ART regimen was continued.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 48-year-old male presenting with polyuria, polydipsia, and fatigue for several days in the setting of severe acute hyperglycemia.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: A 48-year-old male on antiretroviral therapy presented with acute onset of polyuria, polydipsia, and progressive fatigue developing 7 months after transitioning his antiretroviral regimen to include dolutegravir. He had no symptoms of antecedent infection.
subjective.past_medical_history: Underlying retroviral condition on long-term antiretroviral therapy (treated with AZT-3TC-EFV and cotrimoxazole preventive therapy for 10 years, transitioned to tenofovir, lamivudine, and dolutegravir [TDF-3TC-DTG]); baseline fasting blood sugar was 101 mg/dL prior to switch; hypertension treated with amlodipine 10 mg daily; history of cutaneous fungal infection; no personal or family history of diabetes mellitus or dyslipidemia.
subjective.review_of_systems: Polyuria, polydipsia, fatigue; denies fever, chills, cough, abdominal pain, nausea, or vomiting.

objective.routine_investigations: Blood glucose: Random blood sugar (RBS) 320-466 mg/dL; glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) 9.3%. Urinalysis: Ketonuria (3+). (Serum C-peptide, anti-insulin antibodies, and anti-GAD antibodies were not determined due to limited resource setup).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: New-onset diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) and secondary diabetes mellitus precipitated by dolutegravir (DTG) exposure in a patient with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV; diagnosed 11 years previously with stage II disease and baseline CD4 175 cells/mm3, virologically suppressed on ART) and hypertension.
Plan & Outcome: Acute DKA managed with aggressive intravenous fluids, regular insulin infusion, and intravenous potassium chloride, with full resolution of ketoacidosis after 4 days of admission. Transitioned to subcutaneous NPH insulin (20 IU morning / 10 IU evening), subsequently switched to oral metformin 850 mg daily. The DTG-based ART regimen (TDF-3TC-DTG) was maintained. Good glycemic control was achieved on metformin monotherapy (fasting blood sugar 101-130 mg/dL, repeat HbA1c 7.1%).
